questions.question: Which statement is the core engineering test for a useful QML advantage?
options: It survives input preparation and measurement costs while beating a strong classical baseline at matched quality
The circuit uses superposition
The simulator reports a shorter circuit depth
The model contains more qubits than features
questions.explanation: A useful claim is end to end. It includes data access, execution, measurement, output, quality, and a competitive comparator.

questions.question: A Pauli expectation estimate has too much independent sampling uncertainty. Approximately how many more shots halve its confidence-interval width?
options: Four times as many
Twice as many
Eight times as many
The same number
questions.explanation: Independent sampling error decreases with 1/sqrt(shots), so halving the width requires about four times the shots.

questions.question: Why can increasing shots fail to recover the noise-free expectation?
options: More shots reduce sampling error but do not remove systematic device bias
Measurements return every amplitude after enough shots
Shot count only affects classical models
All quantum noise is independent and zero-mean
questions.explanation: A precise estimate of a biased hardware distribution can remain far from the noise-free target.

questions.question: What does a variational quantum training loop usually alternate?
options: Measured circuit evaluations and classical parameter updates
Quantum database writes and cache invalidation
Only deterministic matrix multiplication
Error correction and dataset deletion
questions.explanation: The quantum processor estimates observables or losses, while a classical optimizer proposes new circuit parameters.

questions.question: Which benchmark boundary is required before making an end-to-end advantage claim?
options: Inputs, compilation, queues, measurements, mitigation, repetitions, and classical optimization
The fastest circuit execution from one run
Simulator time without state preparation
Only the number of logical gates
questions.explanation: Leaving out surrounding work can turn an expensive hybrid workflow into an artificially fast circuit-only result.

questions.question: Why is quantum-native data a distinct QML opportunity?
options: A quantum processor may analyze the state without first reconstructing its full classical description
It guarantees fault-tolerant computation
It eliminates measurement uncertainty
It makes every classical baseline invalid
questions.explanation: Quantum-native inputs can avoid one classical loading or tomography bottleneck, although every useful advantage still requires evidence.
